No question right now

Why keep the refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, with the access token in memory?

1So injected scripts can't read the refresh tokenThe browser can still send the cookie with a request.
2So cross-site requests cannot reach the serverThe browser blocks a request before it is sent.
3So the refresh token cannot appear in server logsThe cookie is kept out of all request headers.
4So the access token can be revoked immediatelyThe browser checks each token before a request.

The name

The archer who taught himself

01

Refused a teacher

In the Mahabharata, Drona taught archery to princes. Ekalavya, a forest hunter's son, asked to learn and was turned away.

02

Practiced before a statue

He made a clay statue of Drona and practiced before it, arrow after arrow, until he became a skilled archer.

03

Here, the statue talks back

You learn beside an agent that writes code. Eklavya asks about that work, explains your answers and remembers what you've learned.
